description: Research + record: Aero Hand on the reBot Arm B601. Context to save in plans/: we own the open-source Aero Hand from Chestnut Robotics (formerly Tether AI / TetherIA; docs https://docs.tetheria.ai/docs/GUI). Jake wants to mount it on the Seeed reBot Arm B601-DM (https://www.seeedstudio.com/reBot-Arm-B601-DM-Body-Motor-Kit-p-6752.html; 6+1 DoF, Damiao motors, ~US$1,899 assembled, rated around 2.5 kg payload, to be confirmed). Answer, with sources: (1) Would it work: mechanical mount and flange, wiring, power, control/SDK integration (ROS2/LeRobot), and how the hand's mass cuts into the arm's payload. (2) Usable payload at the hand: arm-rated payload minus hand mass, at what reach, and the hand's own grip force and finger payload limits. (3) What tasks it would do well and badly, focused on automated kitchen food prep (picking produce, holding a knife, stirring, pouring, opening containers, plating), plus what would need a second arm or a different end effector. (4) Which open models (MolmoAct2, pi0/GR00T, etc.) support a dexterous hand on this arm, and how much data would be needed. Write plans/aero_hand_on_b601.md and give Jake a short spoken-style verdict.

results.identified_issue: Plan only, no code. Facts checked 2026-10-17: Seeed RS LeRobot wiki (seeed_b601_rs_follower over socketcan can0; leader rebot_arm_102_leader on ttyUSB); the lerobot-robot-seeed-b601 README (robstride adapter not yet supported, RS config still being refined); the OpenELAB RS structure-kit parts list (no wrist plate named, 'without gripper'); RobotShop Star Arm 102 (.90, 12 V). Unverified: whether macOS can drive the RS at all (I assumed not, since SocketCAN is Linux-only); the RS wrist RobStride model and its torque (the §3 wrist check still uses the DM4310); the RS 48 V supply rating; the J6 flange bolt pattern. The forearm-cuff teleop is my suggestion, not Jake's. The arm is mounted as a left arm because the Aero was flashed left-hand on 2026-10-17 (third_party/aero_hand/README.md).
results.summary: Added your six-step Aero Hand on B601-RS integration plan to plans/aero_hand_on_b601.md, with two catches: the RS needs a Linux computer, and your hand can't grip the leader arm and do webcam fingers at once
results.detailed_description:
Done. Your six steps are now section A at the top of plans/aero_hand_on_b601.md, written for the 48 V RS. The old DM research is still below it, and the doc says where the RS changes the numbers. The biggest change is payload: about 2 kg at the hand instead of about 1.

What I checked, and two catches.

Wrist plate: the RS body structure kit is sold without a gripper, and its parts list doesn't name a wrist plate. So asking Seeed is the right call. I wrote out the exact question (do they include the J6 flange, and can we get its STEP file). If the answer is no, we print that part too.

Power: the hand needs about 60 W, so the buck converter is 48 V in, 6 V out, at least 10 A. That's only about 1.3 A from the arm's supply, so buy a 48 V supply with about 60 W of spare capacity. Put a fuse ahead of the converter and a capacitor after it, because a voltage dip makes the hand re-home itself mid-move.

USB hub: fine. Put it at the base so only the hand's cable and its 6 V lead cross the wrist roll.

Catch one: Seeed's RS LeRobot driver talks to the arm through Linux SocketCAN, and its RobStride adapter is marked not yet supported. So the Mac probably can't run the arm directly. Plan on a Linux box, Pi or Jetson, or ask Seeed for a Mac option.

LeRobot: Seeed already has a plugin for the RS arm and one for the Star Arm 102 leader. So the robot class wraps Seeed's arm class and the Aero SDK instead of rewriting them: a 13-number action, the two eye-height stereo cameras, a torque clamp for long holds, and an over-temperature release.

Catch two, on teleop: the hand holding the leader arm can't also make finger shapes for the webcam. I recommend swapping the leader's handle for a printed forearm cuff, so your left arm drives the arm and your left fingers drive the hand. Our Aero is a left hand, so mount the arm on the left. The fallback is right hand on the leader and left hand in front of the webcam.

Recording uses the normal lerobot-record command with the two new types. The first task stays the same: about 50 gloved demos of picking a vegetable into a bowl, trained with ACT. The doc ends with a shopping and questions list.
results.user_reply_draft: Hey Jake, the RS integration plan is written up in plans/aero_hand_on_b601.md, with your six steps in order. Two things to sort out before buying: ask Seeed whether the RS structure kit includes the wrist plate, and plan on a Linux computer for the arm, because Seeed's RS driver uses Linux-only CAN. Also, we'll want a forearm cuff on the leader arm so your fingers are free for the webcam.

results.notes:
Jake: add this integration plan for the Aero Hand on the reBot B601-RS (he's buying the RS, 48 V):
1. A 3D-printed adapter plate on the wrist flange, replacing the gripper. Confirm with Seeed that the structure kit includes the wrist plate.
2. A 48-to-6 V buck converter on the arm feeding the hand from the arm's supply, so only one power lead runs along the arm.
3. A small USB hub on the arm carrying the hand's USB and the arm's USB-CAN, so one cable goes to the computer.
4. A LeRobot robot class that combines the reBot and the Aero Hand (SDK), with two eye-height cameras (human-mirror principle).
5. Teleop: the leader arm (Star Arm 102) drives the arm, and the webcam hand teleop (teleop.py) drives the hand.
6. Record demonstrations into LeRobot datasets, then train policies.

results.identified_issue: Desk research only; nothing mounted or run. Unverified: current assembled B601-DM price; stock gripper mass (used to claim payload-neutral swap); whether the 1.5 kg rating holds with the wrist horizontal (my 2.6 N·m wrist-torque estimate uses guessed lever arms); the Aero hardware license (one listing says non-commercial); and the data counts, which are extrapolated from a G1+BrainCo GR00T fine-tune (~200/task) and an AVerMedia GR00T-on-B601 blog (~100 demos for gripper pick-place). The Aero docs' mechanical page is a placeholder, so the M3 hole spacing must come from Onshape. Thermal numbers come from docs.tetheria.ai hardware_faq.
results.summary: Researched the Aero Hand on the reBot B601-DM: it works, as a ~1 kg light-duty produce and plating station; full plan in plans/aero_hand_on_b601.md
results.detailed_description:
Short verdict: yes, it bolts on and it'll work, but as a light-duty hand. Two corrections first. The 2.5 kg payload is the B601-RS; the DM version you linked is rated 1.5 kg, and that's without a gripper. And the link is the $995 Body Motor Kit, not the assembled arm (I couldn't confirm the current assembled price).

How it attaches: one adapter plate replaces the stock gripper (the Aero Hand has four M3 inserts on its wrist pad, and both sides have open CAD). Then two new cables run up the arm: 6 V at up to 10 A for the hand, plus a USB cable. Software-wise, we'd write one LeRobot robot class that combines the arm's CAN bus and the hand's USB serial into a 13-number action. The hand has no LeRobot driver of its own.

Payload: about 1 kg at the hand within roughly half a metre of the base. The hand is probably no heavier than the stock gripper, so the swap costs nothing. With the wrist held out flat, the wrist motor caps you around 0.5 to 0.8 kg for sustained work. The surprise limit is heat: if the hand clamps at its default force it overheats in about 2 minutes and can drop what it's holding. So holding a knife or a spoon for long periods needs a lower torque setting and breaks.

Kitchen: good at picking produce, plating and garnishing. OK at small pours and short stirring. Lids work if something else holds the jar. Bad at knife work, pots and heavy bowls. The hand also isn't food-safe (printed PLA with exposed tendons), so it needs a glove, and data should be collected with the glove on. For real food prep, add a second B601 with its stock gripper to hold things, and use a fixed knife or slicer instead of having the hand hold a knife.

Models: GR00T N1.6/1.7 is the best fit for a dexterous hand, and someone has already run GR00T on a B601. Pi0 and pi0.5 also accept the extra action dimensions, and ACT/SmolVLA work as cheap baselines. MolmoAct2 doesn't support a hand out of the box. Data: roughly 50 to 100 demos per task if the hand runs a few fixed grasps, and about 200 per task for full finger control. Suggested first milestone: pick a vegetable into a bowl with a gloved grasp, ACT, about 50 demos.

user_request.name: Add to Helping Hands: Chestnut Robotics, called Tether AI at the time, makes an open source Aero Hand, we have that. I'm interested in attaching it to the reBot arm B601. How would that work, would it work well, what payload could it carry attached to that arm, and what tasks would it do? I'm specifically interested in automated kitchen food prep.

summary: Add an integration plan for mounting the Aero Hand on the 48 V reBot B601-RS: printed wrist adapter, buck-converter power, USB hub, LeRobot robot class with two cameras, leader-arm and webcam teleop, and dataset recording. The plan should replace the earlier B601-DM assumption, and confirm with Seeed that the structure kit includes the wrist plate.
